plan_a_advantages: Dedicated tempo session for speed development
Longer, controlled runs for building endurance and trail durability
plan_b_advantages: More consistent volume of easy runs
Potentially better for recovery due to the emphasis on maintaining freshness
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a more targeted approach to building aerobic base and threshold strength, crucial for improving speed on trails. Plan B focuses heavily on maintaining freshness and volume, which is good for recovery but doesn't prioritize the specific adaptations needed for faster running. Plan A’s inclusion of a dedicated tempo session and longer, controlled efforts directly addresses the goal of increasing running speed, while Plan B’s longer, moderate-intensity runs could potentially lead to over-reliance on endurance without significant speed gains. Furthermore, the shorter, more frequent easy runs in Plan A allow for better recovery and adaptation between harder sessions.
